title: Session tiling and slimline tool handoff playbook
content:
Purpose

This is a working playbook for a lightweight "session tiling" approach to hosted streaming sessions that must interoperate cleanly with tool calls and structured output. The goal is pragmatic: reduce end-to-end latency and client complexity for mobile/edge SDKs while preserving resumability and deterministic tool-handshake semantics. This doc is deliberately tactical (field notes + small API sketches) rather than a canonical PRD.

Background / motivation

We have many hosted API projects leaning on heavy session snapshotting or full transcript replay when network flaps or clients move between networks. Those approaches are robust but expensive (token and latency cost) and awkward for client SDKs. At the same time, tool calling semantics (idempotency, commit/abort, partial results) need clearer low-latency primitives for thin clients. Session tiling aims to split a long-running conversation into small, resumable "tiles" with minimal metadata so clients can switch between offline/online modes without replaying large prefixes.

High-level goals
- Keep per-tile handshake under 200ms for common mobile RTTs (target median end-to-end 120ms for tile-init + warm KV).
- Provide deterministic tool-call commits across tiling boundaries (no partial-dupe tool side-effects).
- Minimize client memory/compute: SDK should prefer metadata pointers and compact deltas over full transcript replay.
- Make structured-output contracts (JSON frames or typed events) available incrementally so clients can show partial UI while tool calls resolve.

Non-goals
- Not attempting complex offline-first conflict-resolution (CRDTs) in this phase. We assume single-writer session model.
- Not replacing server-side long-term retention or audit logs — tiles are an operational primitive, not the canonical provenance store.

Assumptions
- Customers already send session_id with every call. We will reuse this existing identifier for tiles.
- Tool backends expose an idempotency key surface and can accept a commit/abort plan keyed by a tile_id.
- KV cache warmups are possible if we reuse short-lived tile-level cache keys.

Concepts & primitives
- Tile: small contiguous chunk of session activity (e.g., N tokens or M seconds). Contains a compact metadata header and optional compressed delta of recent user messages.
- Tile header: {tile_id, prev_tile_id, seq_start, seq_end, resume_nonce, schema_version} (we will standardize names later). Keep header <1KB.
- Resume nonce: ephemeral anti-replay token generated by server for tile resumptions; tied to an authentication window.
- Tool intent frame: ephemeral descriptor emitted by the model when a tool call is required. Includes tool_id, args_hash, suggested_idempotency_key.
- Commit envelope: when a tile that contains tool intents completes, the SDK can request a commit check before presenting the result. Server replies with commit_token which the SDK uses when actuating side-effecting calls.

API sketches
1) Open a tile (SDK -> server)
POST /v1/sessions/{session_id}/tiles
body: {client_clock, prev_tile_id?, client_capabilities: ["typed-json","delta-compression"], hint_max_tokens}
response: {tile_id, resume_nonce, kv_cache_key, expected_schema_version}

2) Stream frames into a tile (server streaming)
frame kinds we support: USER_CHUNK, MODEL_DELTA, TOOL_INTENT, TOOL_RESULT, CHECKPOINT
Client can send USER_CHUNK frames; server yields MODEL_DELTA and TOOL_INTENT frames. Each frame has a small tile_offset.

3) Complete and request commit check
POST /v1/sessions/{session_id}/tiles/{tile_id}/complete
body: {summary_hint, final_offsets, want_commit_check: true|false}
response: {commit_candidates: [ {tool_id, args_hash, can_commit: true|false, reason}], commit_token?}

4) Execute tool with commit token
POST /v1/tools/{tool_id}/execute
headers: {x-commit-token: <commit_token>} 
body: {idempotency_key, args}
response: tool-specific result (server validates binding between commit_token and idempotency_key)

SDK ergonomics guidance
- Thin-by-default: SDKs should store only last 2 tiles locally and a tile-index that lists prev/next. Older tiles may be offloaded to disk or remote storage provided by the app.
- Optimistic UI: when MODEL_DELTA frames arrive with a TOOL_INTENT, SDK should surface a non-final preview in a specialized UI slot and mark it "pending tool". When TOOL_RESULT arrives, swap and animate commit.
- Automatic hedging: if client detects high upstream latency (>400ms), SDK may speculatively call a non-side-effecting local fallback to keep UI snappy, but must label fallback outputs clearly.
- Retry semantics: SDK must surface a single retry helper that maps to server-side idempotency keys. Avoid trying to auto-retry tool execution that the server marked non-idempotent.

Structured output & schema migration
- We will support a typed event envelope with schema_version in tile header.
- Server can emit progressive typed fragments (e.g., partial JSON object with a path) and a finalization event. SDKs should assemble partial fragments into a delta view.
- Migration: when schema_version changes, server should provide a lightweight transformation hint so SDK can render older tiles gracefully (fallback to plain text if necessary).

Operational concerns
- Cost: Tiles increase metadata operations. We expect a 5–12% increase in metadata requests for long sessions vs. naive replay; acceptable tradeoff for latency savings. We'll track per-session PUTs and commit checks.
- Observability: add tile-level traces to the Console (latency histogram, per-tile commit-check outcome, tool commit failures). Ensure we can trace from commit_token -> tool execution -> final result.
- Security: commit_tokens are short-lived (TTL ~60s) and bound to session + requester fingerprint; leak-resistant by design. Resume nonces must be rotated on explicit logins and on revocation.

Success metrics (initial)
- Median tile-init latency <= 120ms in mobile-regional tests.
- Mean number of resumed bytes per reconnect <= 2KB (we want compact resumes, not transcript replay).
- Tool commit failure rate after commit_token issuance < 0.5% in first month.
- SDK error rate on resume < 1% of sessions.

Rollout plan (0 -> GA)
- Alpha: internal SDK + canary customers; no automatic resume; commit checks opt-in (2 weeks).
- Beta: enable resume for 10% of sessions, gather telemetry, add QA for tool commit flows (4 weeks).
- GA: enable by default with migration notes and clear SDK versioning (after beta stabilization).

Open questions / TODOs
- How do we reconcile multi-device single-writer assumptions with common use cases where user opens same session on laptop+phone? (We might need a quick-lock mechanism.)
- Decide exact tile sizing heuristic: token-based vs. time-based vs. hybrid. Need perf experiments.
- Server-side storage TTL for tiles: what default retention for quick resume (30m? 24h?). Tradeoffs between cost and UX.
- Backpressure: how will server signal that tile-init must be rejected or deferred under heavy load? Design a precise retry-after + degrade-to-full-replay path.

Next steps
- Perf spike tests: implement tile-init in runtime trace harness, measure median under typical mobile RTT distributions (Benches by 2025-02-21).
- Spec review with serving-runtime and SRE: confirm commit_token validation steps and expiry behavior. (Owner: Ethan Park)
- Small SDK spike: implement JS/mobile proof-of-concept that keeps two tiles in memory and shows optimistic tool-preview slots. (Owner: Maya Gupta)

Notes to reviewers
- This is an intentionally small-surface intervention: think of tiles as a lightweight operational primitive. If this pattern looks promising we can expand into richer session partitioning and multi-writer CRDTs later.
- I'm calling this "slimline" to emphasize minimal client memory/latency for first wave. Please add comments inline or drop notes in #hosted-api.
